recipes.name: Hot Pepper Sauce - A Trinidadian Staple
ingredients_raw: 1 small mango - peeled, seeded, and cut into chunks

steps.text: Wearing disposable gloves, and being careful not to get any in your eyes or on your skin, roughly chop the habanero peppers. Place the habanero peppers, mango, onion, green onions, and garlic into a blender. Pour in the vinegar, lime juice, and vegetable oil, cover the blender, and pulse until the mixture is very finely chopped. Stop the blender, and add dry mustard powder, salt, curry powder, and lime zest. Blend again until the sauce is smooth. Pour into clean jars, and store in refrigerator.

raw_recipe.headline: Hot Pepper Sauce - A Trinidadian Staple
raw_recipe.description: Fiery hot habanero peppers -- 15 of them! -- make this volcanic hot sauce something to remember. Use rubber gloves to chop and seed the fiendish pods.

review.reviewBody: I made this Pepper Sauce today, and I must say...it is the hottest I've ever had! But here's the difference...it also has a lot of flavor. Some people like just heat; but if there's no flavor, then it's no different than a mouthful of fire. I didn't change anything at all since it was my first time making it. But maybe next time I will use just 10 habaneros so some of my friends will be able to eat it without bursting into flames! Thanks for a great recipe.

I wanted this to work very badly so I followed the instructions to the letter. I even had the missus help me out.

The recipe made 4 1/2 cups and smelled putrid. I blended, mixed and even put it through the grinder to try and "thin-it-out." The concoction was still very thick.

I put it in some chili to see if I mixing it with food would eliminate the smell and add some flavor. No way! The overpowering MUSTARD taste and smell was still present.

Think about it, a quarter cup of Dry Mustard. Perhaps if it was eliminated the recipe might be good. I didn't even use the entire quarter cup because I ran out. 

The mixture tastes like a Vodka Mustard Schnapps.

Great recipe! I used to experiment with different hot sauce recipes then I found this one and I haven't looked back. I use a variety of peppers that I grow in my garden. (habanero, scotch bonnet, Trinidad scorpion, Carolina reaper, ghost)
Changes: Reduce the amount of mustard powder to 2 Tbsp per batch. Blend the peppers whole (I don't remove the seeds). Warm the sauce up to just before boiling then stick blend to achieve a smooth consistency. When the sauce cools I put it in hard plastic bottles that I have sanitized. (Gatorade is perfect)

This is the BEST! I modify it slightly, 10 peppers with the seeds removed, and I add about an inch of ginger root. The mustard I go a little light on, but close to 1/4 cup (which, by the way is the equivalent of 4 Tablespoons). Oh, and Tumeric. It is good for you, and heightens the color. I have given jars to a bunch of friends, and they all rave about it, even the people who are somewhat pepper wimps. One friend hates curry, so I poured some out before adding it and she has been playing around with different spices, so far likes cumin the most. The best thing is how easy it is to whip up. I am so glad I stumbled onto this recipe.

Wow, I feel just like the other reviewers, great taste/flavor to go with the heat. My husband likes the hot sauce in the family and I usually stay away, as most are just fire in your mouth. I made this and it was accepted by everyone. I did not use Habaneros, I have a garden and tons of hot peppers ( 5 or 6 kinds) and was running out of things to do with them - this was fantastic. I really think the Mango and green onion does something for these hot peppers, we have had it on chicken, fried pork chops, with chips, I made a curry meal and we ate it with that. My husband took it to work for others to try, it is gone and I am ready to go and pick some more peppers. You will not be unhappy. Thanks for a great receipe. NOTE: I tried to make this and process it in a pressure cooker like I do other things, it did not taste the same, it was not bad when we opened the jars, but it seemed to be fermenting - tiny bubble inside, not sure why, or what was reacting with what - but it altered the taste, much better fresh - will try freezing some next time I make a batch and see how that does. WE REALLY LIKE THIS SAUCE.

This is my absolute favorite sauce. I put it on nearly anything savory, yet I find it pairs best with pork.
Minor adjustments: I add 1/4 cup of honey, 1 tsp dried ground ginger, 1 tsp liquid smoke, 1 tsp vanilla powder.
Other than that, i follow to the letter. Only fresh mango will do. If I would have to choose canned, I simply will not make it.
This is the best habanero-based sauce I have ever tried, and I highly recommend it to anyone who likes spicy food.
Try it, sez me!

Okay, this is absolutely fantastic.
It is so simple, throw everything in the blender and you come out with the best hot sauce I've ever made or eaten.

My husband wants to put it on everything and I literally had a thought of "okay, wonder if we could turn this into ice cream." Okay, maybe not but it is outstanding. We even take it to restaurants.
 I have made it with multiple kinds of chiles and works beautifully with anything. Also, frozen mangoes, again, works perfectly. If you don't have mustard powder, some plain yellow mustard has worked.

If you are getting something 'putrid' you are doing something wrong wrong wrong.

I am making this sauce again today for the second time in 5 months. My husband loves it! So does my son and I. It is amazing made like buffalo wing sauce. Melt a stick of butter with a cup or so of sauce and simmer. It tones down the heat a little, which is not said as a good or bad thing because obviously people who make this sauce LOVE hot food, it's just simply a fact. It just happens to be that it is an amazing combination warmed with butter, and is fantastic on crispy wings or as a dipping sauce for tenders or grilled chicken (or pork). Trust me, try it. Use as much butter or sauce to your liking-you can't go wrong. Also, this stuff is amazing straight up on mac and cheese! Wow! We are addicted to that combo. Definitely 5 stars!

I always buy hot sauce but didn't have any and my food was ready waiting....,I stumbled on this recipe though didn't have all the ingredients, I used: 
3 x garlic, two thirds of a white onion, 4 x scotch bonnet peppers, teaspoon curry powder, salt and apple cider vinegar, forgot to add the oil, didn't have limes etc. I didn't like the colour (my peppers were yellow and lime green, so added a big squeeze of tomato puree. I took the vinegar harshness away with a little bit of brown sugar. It took less than 5 minutes to make and it is deeeelicious, blew my head off with the heat and flavour. Amazing! thank you! I look forward to following the recipe properly next time, the ingredients are on my shopping list. Though, not sure I need to add the oil - is it necessary?

This sauce is easy to make, just follow the directions. The only thing I did, differently was to blanch the peppers in a half cup of vinegar first, then I continued with the recipe. My family loves hot sauce, and they love that this sauce makes you sit up and notice the food! It has the heat!

This is the third time I am making this sauce. I add scotch bonnet and scorpion peppers this time. Along with Carolina reaper and scorpion pepper sea salt. It has heat but still a lot of yummy flavor .

I am from Trinidad where this type of sauce is a household staple. This recipe was pretty close! I used ‘almost ripe’ mangoes and omitted the mustard and added 1 Scorpion pepper and a few Trinidad pimento peppers for even more flavor. It’s definitely not hot enough for someone who likes things hot, but it’s spicy enough for many more people to enjoy it. Since I used almost ripe mangoes, mine tastes more like a Trinidad mango chutney than a pepper sauce but that’s just right for me. Next time I will use a ripe mango and will add a couple more peppers with higher scoville to bump up the heat a little.

Our adult children love this and ask for more each pepper season. This is my third year making it so far. They use it on sandwiches, dipping chicken, barbequed meats, even eggs and omelets. Definitely a home staple.

This hot sauce is absolutely delicious. My favorite recipe for sure. It’s got the fruity sweetness of mango, the boldness of that mustard, and the heat of habanero. It’s so nuanced with the hint of curry occasionally too. Super easy to make. I store mine in a couple of old Sriracha bottles. Thanks for this!
This is delicious!! Easy to make, wonderfully flavorful and very versatile. We thought it would be hotter than it is - what a wonderful surprise.

Wow!!! This is SOOOO good! It is definately not for the person that doesn't like spicy! If you do like spicy, this is amazing. We put it on our chicken wings and "most" of my family really liked it, but some said way too hot! I acutally used the leftovers on just about everything I could put it on!

My wife was from Trinidad and the first time I had this I was hooked. The main company Matouks of Trinidad makes this and sells it all over the world. It's fairly expensive although I have to say I cannot tell the difference. Every family in Trinidad has its own receipt for Pepper Sauce. Actually it is supposed to be healthy for you and its very low in calories and it enhances almost every food and has you know it does not take a lot. Try it on omelets, sandwiches, fish, and even pizza also adds a kick to the dry instant noddles.
Very hot. Great flavor. I think I'll add more mango to tone down the heat.
a next day update: the flavor really sets in after two days. where the pepper dominates day 1 and 2, on the third day the flavours really deepen
Hot with a unique flavor.
